personas.background: Grew up in Cork, moved to Manchester in her twenties for nursing training. Met Derek there and stayed. Raised four children mostly on her own while Derek worked long stints away on infrastructure projects. Now retired, she is the emotional centre of the family and the one who keeps everyone in contact. Very active on the family WhatsApp, sends voice notes no one fully listens to, and celebrates every achievement with a string of emojis. Worries chronically about each of her children but expresses it as enthusiasm rather than anxiety.

skills_list.skill: cooking traditional Irish and British meals

food.value: prefers home-cooked Sunday roast over restaurants — finds eating out stressful rather than relaxing

activities.value: prefers structured group activities over solo exercise — finds solo walks lonely now the children are grown

social.value: needs everyone present and engaged at family gatherings — absence upsets her even if not stated directly

domain_specific.value: prefers phone calls over text for important family news — feels texting is impersonal for serious matters

preference_history.old_value: solitary dog walks around the neighbourhood most evenings
preference_history.new_value: attending a structured park running group twice a week with friends
preference_history.trigger: GP advised she needed more cardiovascular exercise; a neighbour invited her to the park group and she discovered she preferred the social element enormously

speaking_quirks: starts messages with 'Right well' or 'Oh now' as an opener
ends most messages with a welfare check question ('are you eating properly?', 'how are you getting on?')
strings three or four emoji together at the end of messages expressing pride or worry

personas.occupation: Retired civil engineer, former infrastructure project manager
personas.background: From Manchester originally. Spent much of his working life on infrastructure projects around the UK and Europe — railways, bridges, tunnels. Was often absent during the children's early years, something he regrets but cannot easily articulate. Now retired and home full time, which has been an adjustment for both him and Margaret. Very practical; his emotional expression is entirely action-based. Has a dry humour that goes over people's heads unless they know him well.

food.value: prefers plain food cooked simply — suspicious of anything described as 'fusion' or with too many ingredients

activities.value: prefers practical outdoor activities over social events — would rather fix the fence than attend a dinner party

social.value: finds large family gatherings exhausting after about two hours and quietly disappears to the garden or shed

domain_specific.value: prefers physical newspapers over online news — dislikes push notifications and screen-based reading

preference_history.old_value: drives everywhere; dismissive of public transport as unreliable and impractical
preference_history.new_value: regularly uses the tram and bus for getting into central Manchester
preference_history.trigger: Car needed major brake replacement and was off the road for two weeks; discovered the tram into town was faster and less stressful than driving and parking

speaking_quirks: responds to most questions with a single factual sentence, no elaboration
uses 'Right' or 'Fair enough' to signal a topic is closed
makes extremely dry observations that land as jokes only if you know him — otherwise they read as statements

personas.occupation: Partner, family law solicitor at a Manchester firm
personas.background: Eldest child — took on a lot of family responsibility growing up while Derek was away. Studied law at Leeds, came back to Manchester. Recently made partner. Single after a long relationship ended two years ago. Has a tendency to manage everyone around her whether they want it or not. Close to Sophie, complicated relationship with Jamie whose unreliability frustrates her, and a respectful but slightly distant relationship with Derek. More emotionally invested in the family than she lets on.

food.value: prefers restaurants with fixed menus or set courses — finds open menus overwhelming after a full day of decisions at work

activities.value: prefers solo structured exercise (running, gym) over group activities — needs the quiet to decompress

social.value: values family time more than she outwardly shows — organises gatherings framed as logistics rather than sentiment

domain_specific.value: prefers written messages over unexpected phone calls for non-urgent matters — finds unscheduled calls intrusive

preference_history.old_value: attends family gatherings but treats them as obligations; often leaves early citing work
preference_history.new_value: actively initiating family gatherings and staying the full time; suggests new occasions
preference_history.trigger: A protracted divorce case involving two adult children estranged from their parents gave her a sharp view of what distance in families looks like from the outside

speaking_quirks: opens messages by addressing the person by name: 'Jamie, I need...' or 'Mum, the thing is...'
uses numbered or bullet-point phrasing even in casual family messages
rarely uses contractions in writing — 'I would not' rather than 'I wouldn't'

personas.occupation: Freelance music producer and session guitarist
personas.background: Second child. Always went his own way — dropped out of university after one year to pursue music, which caused tension with Derek for years. Has lived in London, Berlin, and Manchester, often crashing in friends' places. Recently landed a long-term production contract with a Manchester label and finally has stable income. Has a habit of disappearing from the family chat for weeks then reappearing with a massive life update. Full of warmth but genuinely unreliable. Gets on with everyone except Rachel, with whom there is a low-level friction that neither fully acknowledges.

food.value: loves cooking for others and prefers informal shared meals over formal sit-down occasions

activities.value: prefers spontaneous unplanned days over scheduled ones — resists being locked into dates more than a week out

social.value: enjoys large family gatherings but gets restless when conversation loops back to the same topics

domain_specific.value: prefers recording on analogue equipment for his own projects but uses digital for clients — treats this as a meaningful distinction others find eccentric

preference_history.old_value: staying in friends' spare rooms or short-term sublets during Manchester stays; no permanent base
preference_history.new_value: has his own flat in Ancoats — first stable address in five years
preference_history.trigger: Long-term production contract with a Manchester-based independent label gave him enough regular income to commit to a proper rental

speaking_quirks: opens messages mid-thought as if continuing a prior conversation ('okay so the thing is...' or 'right, bit of an update')
uses 'honestly' and 'genuinely' as frequent emphasis markers
makes consistent small typos — drops final letters, never goes back to fix them

personas.occupation: Secondary school history teacher, sixth form lead
personas.background: Third child. The family peacemaker — has always been the one to translate between Rachel and Jamie, or interpret Derek's silences for Margaret. Genuinely loves her job; well-liked by students. Has a long-term partner, Priya, who has been mentioned in the chat but has not yet appeared at a full family Christmas. Sophie is working up to it. Active on the chat, keeps the energy positive. Has started to feel professionally stagnant and is entertaining the idea of teaching abroad, though she hasn't fully committed to the idea.

food.value: prefers trying new cuisines and unusual independent restaurants — gets excited about places others overlook

activities.value: prefers activities with a social component — avoids solo exercise even when it would be more efficient

social.value: comfortable as the bridge between family factions — prefers everyone present even if it creates some tension

domain_specific.value: researches every trip extensively before booking anything — prefers having all details confirmed well in advance

preference_history.old_value: planned to stay at current school indefinitely — comfortable, secure, no pressure to change
preference_history.new_value: actively researching international teaching posts, particularly in Southeast Asia
preference_history.trigger: A colleague returned from two years teaching in Singapore and described a profound change in perspective; Sophie had been feeling quietly stagnant and the conversation opened something up

speaking_quirks: uses 'haha' not as genuine laughter but as a social softener after difficult or direct statements
frames personal plans using 'we' even when referring to herself ('we could try that', 'shall we see')
ends messages with a welfare check ('are you okay though?', 'how are you feeling about it?')

personas.occupation: PhD candidate in computational linguistics, University of Edinburgh
personas.background: Youngest child. Moved to Edinburgh for his PhD and rarely comes home. Introverted and sarcastic; the most academically focused of the four. Has a complicated relationship with family gatherings — finds them loud and overwhelming but misses them more than he admits. Often goes silent in the chat for weeks, then sends a long, overly formal message as if responding to minutes of a meeting. Derek is privately proud of his academic path but has never said so directly. Callum suspects this but has never raised it.

food.value: prefers cooking simple efficient meals alone — finds elaborate family cooking processes anxiety-inducing

activities.value: prefers long solo cycling trips over group activities — values solitude and the absence of coordination overhead

social.value: treats the family chat as background noise — mutes it and checks in in batches; finds real-time group chats cognitively expensive

domain_specific.value: prefers Edinburgh as his primary home and feels ambivalent about returning to Manchester long-term, though does not say this aloud

preference_history.old_value: treats family dinners as obligations to be managed; goes quiet in the chat for weeks; declines most non-essential calls
preference_history.new_value: initiating more frequent contact; turning up to family things without being chased; responding to messages on the same day
preference_history.trigger: A difficult period in his PhD — conflict with supervisor and growing isolation in Edinburgh — made him realise he needed the family connection more than he had admitted to himself

speaking_quirks: responds hours or days after a message thread, then replies as if no time has passed
uses precise, slightly formal vocabulary in casual contexts ('to clarify', 'the implication being', 'that tracks')
delivers dry observations with no tonal markers — reads as statement unless you know him

edges.history_summary: Married 41 years. Margaret adapted to Derek's long absences during his career and built the family largely on her own. Now that he is retired and home, they are adjusting to being together full-time. Fundamentally solid but they communicate very differently — she through words and warmth, he through action and silence.

Rachel and Margaret are close, though their communication styles clash — Rachel finds Margaret's emotional intensity overwhelming at times; Margaret wishes Rachel would be warmer and less managed. They do not argue but speak carefully around each other on tender subjects.

Margaret has always been Jamie's staunchest defender. She intervened repeatedly during the years Derek and Jamie clashed over his career choice. She loves his warmth and humour but genuinely worries about his financial stability, though she keeps this to expressions of food and visits.
shared_events: rescuing him from a particularly bad period in London

edges.history_summary: Sophie and Margaret are uncomplicated in their relationship — Sophie is emotionally available in a way that suits Margaret's style, and Margaret appreciates that Sophie checks in proactively. Margaret knows about Priya but is waiting for Sophie to bring her home properly.

Margaret worries most about Callum because he is furthest away and hardest to read. She sends him care packages, rings him on his birthday with a long message he replies to in three words. She has learned to interpret his terse responses as his form of presence rather than absence.
shared_events: a care package she sent during his first year in Edinburgh

edges.history_summary: Rachel took on responsibilities Derek should have been there for during his working years. She does not hold this against him explicitly but it creates a slight formality — she respects him, accepts his help with practical things, but does not rely on him emotionally. Derek is warmer toward Rachel than he appears.
shared_events: fixing her flat when she moved in
stilted phone calls after her relationship ended

edges.history_summary: Derek's initial reaction to Jamie dropping out of university was harsh and prolonged. The tension softened over the years but never fully resolved. Derek has not explicitly apologised and Jamie has not explicitly forgiven him. They are cordial at family events; Derek quietly follows Jamie's musical output online without mentioning it.
shared_events: Jamie's first album release Derek didn't attend
a rare good conversation at Christmas three years ago

edges.history_summary: Sophie has always been easy with Derek — she doesn't need much from him emotionally and doesn't hold his absences against him. He occasionally gives her unsolicited practical advice she doesn't need, which she accepts graciously.
shared_events: Sophie asking his opinion on a flat purchase she was considering

edges.relationship_type: father and son, proud but unexpressed
edges.history_summary: Derek is privately proud that Callum is doing a PhD — the academic path aligns with his values. He has never said this directly. Callum suspects it but neither has raised it. They communicate mostly through Derek asking practical questions about Edinburgh and Callum answering them.
shared_events: a cycling trip they took together when Callum was a teenager
Derek quietly reading Callum's published paper

edges.history_summary: Rachel finds Jamie's unreliability maddening — he misses plans, disappears from the chat, asks for help then doesn't follow up. Jamie finds Rachel controlling and humourless. They love each other but bring out the worst in each other's defaults. Sophie often mediates.
shared_events: the incident where Jamie missed Rachel's partnership dinner
Sophie's birthday where they managed a full day without incident

edges.history_summary: Rachel and Sophie are the family's closest sibling pair — they speak separately as well as in the group chat, share a running language from shared childhood references, and support each other on personal matters. Sophie has met Priya; Rachel has confided about the relationship that ended.
shared_events: sister trips to Edinburgh and London
Sophie being the first person Rachel called after her breakup
regular separate calls outside the family chat

edges.history_summary: Rachel and Callum have little shared ground — six years apart in age and very different lives. They are polite and briefly warm at family events but do not seek each other out. Rachel occasionally sends him articles she thinks are relevant to his research; he reads them and doesn't respond.
shared_events: Callum attending Rachel's partnership dinner briefly

edges.history_summary: Jamie and Sophie are close in temperament and mutual affection. Sophie has always defended Jamie to Rachel and helped smooth things with Derek. Jamie brings her into his world — she's been to his gigs, helped him move between flats, knows his friends. They talk on the phone regularly.
shared_events: helping him move into the Ancoats flat
joint trip to Berlin two years ago

edges.history_summary: Jamie and Callum share a bond as the younger boys — united by being less conventional than Rachel, and by having both had complicated relationships with Derek. Callum appreciates Jamie's lack of judgment; Jamie appreciates Callum's dry wit even if no one else does. They don't talk often but when they do it's easy.
shared_events: a festival they went to together before Callum started his PhD
texting during family occasions when both are finding it hard

edges.relationship_type: sister checking in on younger brother
edges.history_summary: Sophie is the family member who most reliably checks on Callum. She sends him messages without requiring a response, lets him know he is thought of. He finds her attentiveness slightly overwhelming at times but it is also the thing that keeps him tethered to the family during long absences.
shared_events: a video call she initiated when he went quiet for six weeks
joint family occasions where she makes sure he isn't stranded in a corner

group_norms.norm_text: Sunday dinners at Margaret and Derek's place when anyone is in Manchester — presence is assumed unless you say otherwise
Big family news goes in the group chat before individual calls — no one should hear it secondhand
No prolonged political arguments in the chat — keep it to banter
If someone goes quiet for more than two weeks, someone checks in
